title: Distinct sources of decision-related signals in visual cortex are represented in different local field potential bands
experiments_summary: Four adult female rhesus macaque monkeys performed one of two perceptual decision-making tasks: two monkeys performed a random dot motion discrimination task (area MT recordings) and two performed a match-to-sample form discrimination task (area V4 recordings). Neural activity was recorded using 16-contact linear V-Probes yielding both single-unit spikes and LFPs. LFP signals were re-referenced, line noise at 60 Hz removed, and power spectra computed via multi-taper Fourier methods (Chronux toolbox). Choice probability (CP) was computed from LFP power distributions across three canonical frequency bands (alpha-beta: 5–30 Hz; low-gamma: 30–70 Hz; high-gamma: 70–150 Hz) and three trial epochs (baseline: −200–0 ms; stimulus-response: 50–250 ms; delay: 250–400 ms post-stimulus onset). Because LFP power is non-normally distributed, a robust scaling normalization (median and IQR) was used instead of z-scoring, validated via simulations with the NeuroDSP toolbox. CP was then estimated via ROC analysis. To test causal contributions, muscimol (GABAA agonist, ~10 mg/mL, ~2 µl) was infused through the probe's fluid channel in 14 paired sessions, with pre- and post-inactivation blocks collected on the same day. Behavioral performance was equated across conditions by selecting matched stimulus difficulty levels. Statistical comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank (WSR) and Wilcoxon rank-sum (WRS) tests, and linear mixed-effects ANOVAs (CP ~ epoch × condition + (1|monkey)). CP latency was estimated via a threshold-free two-segment change-point model. A linear decoder (L2-regularized logistic regression with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, 20 repeats) was trained on high-gamma LFP features to classify stimulus identity and assess stimulus coding before and after inactivation. A population geometry analysis was performed by extracting a decoder-defined stimulus axis, projecting it out of the population activity matrix, and applying PCA to the residual to define a null (orthogonal) dimension; spectral loading energy was computed for each axis across frequency bands. Reward history effects on alpha-beta CP were examined by separating trials based on whether the immediately preceding trial was rewarded or not. Laminar depth dependence of CP was assessed using linear slope and superficial-deep contrast metrics across probe contacts. Saline control injections verified that inactivation effects were attributable to muscimol and not to injection mechanics.
